title: Product Manager — Kits and Integrated Workflows
description:
At ONI, we are driven by a profound mission: to propel scientific discovery and combat diseases by granting everyone the ability to visualize, comprehend, and share the intricate microscopic details of life. Our revolutionary Nanoimager and Aplo Platform stand at the forefront of advancing cellular studies on a molecular level, making substantial contributions to the evolution of scientific knowledge. 

We’re looking for a product manager to own our kits and workflows, including EV Profiler and LNP Profiler, now that the concept is proven. You’ll make sure sample preparation, fluid handling, imaging, analysis and reporting software work together as one system, and your responsibility is the complete customer experience, from sample to scientifically meaningful result. The job is making that system rock solid: hardening what’s already on the market, making sure it works the same way at every site, and getting more customers on it without support load growing at the same rate. 


The Role

As part of the Product team, you’ll own the product management of our kits and end-to-end workflows, including the Discovery Kit, EV Profiler and LNP Profiler and their future revisions. You will ensure these work together with automated sample preparation and fluid handling, imaging, analysis and reporting software to deliver reliable, reproducible and intuitive solutions for our customers.  

The initial products have launched, and the work now is making them dependable, repeatable, and scalable for our customers. You’ll create clarity and momentum for the R&D teams by understanding which problems matter, turning customer and market evidence into priorities, and removing barriers to delivering a coherent solution. You’ll grow adoption to routine use across many sites, including bioprocessing and QC settings where results must be reproducible and defensible, and you’ll work with Marketing on positioning and the product story as the portfolio evolves. You will play a critical role in bringing these quality improvements to the market and ensuring that current and future kits maintain their quality over time, and you’ll help define the roadmap for next iterations of existing and future kits and workflows. As a product manager, you’ll be the connective tissue between software, hardware, bioware, support, and the field, acting as the voice of the customer to help internal teams better understand our customers’ needs and problems.  

The role is ideal for a technically curious, commercially aware individual who loves getting hands-on with products, takes ownership of outcomes and thrives on complex, cross-functional challenges. You will work broadly across our platform and alongside US colleagues; the position is based in Oxford and involves occasional travel to customers and our US team (typically 10-20%). 


What you’ll do

  • Understand scientists and their complete workflows first-hand. Work with customers and field teams, study usage and support data, and synthesize their sometimes conflicting inputs into the problems worth solving. 

  • Drive evidence-led product direction and priorities across our solutions with R&D and commercial leaders, balancing customer outcomes, differentiation, adoption, reliability, margin and technical feasibility. 

  • Own the roadmap for our kits (including the Discovery Kit and the EV and LNP Profiler kits) and workflows, balancing quality, reliability, usability and new features. 

  • Build and refine market and product requirements (MRD/PRD) across workflows, from sample preparation (Aplo Flow) through acquisition (Aplo Scope) to analysis (CODI), according to our Product Development Process. 

  • Own validation for each kit and workflow: define acceptance criteria, performance specifications and validation plans, including reference samples and reproducibility across instruments, operators and sites. Work with R&D, who own development and verification. 

  • Drive coherence across our end-to-end solutions, ensuring kits, reagents, lab automation, instruments and software evolve together rather than as disconnected products. Champion reproducibility, usability and reliable results across the complete workflow. 

  • Connect R&D, operations, quality, service, field applications, sales, marketing and customers. Establish feedback loops, clear ownership and effective cross-team decisions. 

  • Own pricing and packaging for our kits and workflows, balancing customer value, competitiveness and margin targets. 

  • Work with Marketing throughout a product's life to shape positioning, the value proposition and the product story as the portfolio evolves, not only at launch. 

  • Lead launch and release planning with R&D, Marketing and the field: set readiness criteria, make go/no-go decisions, and coordinate documentation, release notes and training for each launch or revision. 

  • Create and run webinars and internal training for the field application and sales teams on new products and revisions, and keep an accurate record of what each kit, instrument and software version can deliver. 

  • Track post-launch performance, including adoption, kit reorders, time to first result, reproducibility, support burden, customer feedback and commercial results, and use it to set priorities. 

  • Analyze support tickets, logs and customer feedback to identify recurring failure modes, and prioritize root-cause fixes into the roadmap. 

  • Work with Quality and Operations on manufacturing transfer, life cycle support and end of life, so our kits and workflows maintain quality over time. 


What you’ll bring

  • A life-science background, ideally EVs, LNPs, nanoparticle characterization, imaging or biophysics. Being able to speak the language of our customers is critical. An MSc/PhD or equivalent hands-on experience is a real plus. 

  • Fluency across software, instruments, laboratory workflows and multidisciplinary R&D; comfortable investigating issues hands-on and understanding how the system fits together. 

  • Experience working with empowered, cross-functional development teams: knowing when to provide context, decide on a trade-off and leave the solution to specialists. 

  • Product management (or product owner) experience in life-science tools or instrumentation, ideally taking something from first release to a scaled, supported product.  

  • Experience planning and running launches with Marketing, R&D and the field, from development through adoption. 

  • Commercial and pricing judgement: You can weigh customer value, competitiveness and margin when setting price and packaging. 

  • A quality mindset: You’re comfortable writing acceptance criteria and test plans, and you think about risk, reproducibility and traceability. Exposure to a quality system (ISO 9001 or 13485) is a plus. 

  • Comfort with data: logs, tickets, precision and method-comparison numbers (CVs, site to site). Evidence sets priorities, not the loudest voice. 

  • The ability to lead across software, hardware, bioware, support and field without owning any of them, and to prioritize when everything feels urgent. 

  • Clear writing and organization skills. Requirements, release notes and docs that other people can act on. 


Nice to have

  • Super-resolution or single-molecule imaging experience (dSTORM, PALM, DNA-PAINT), or general microscopy experience (TIRF, widefield, confocal, spinning-disk). 

  • Hands-on EV or LNP work in research, biopharma, gene therapy or drug delivery. 

  • Laboratory automation, automated liquid handling, sample preparation, consumable kits, workflow integration, scientific software or data analysis. 

  • Integrating instruments, software, consumables and automated lab workflows; exposure to verification, validation, quality systems or lifecycle support. 

  • Commercialization, pricing, segmentation, product positioning or product marketing in technically sophisticated markets.

When you become a part of our team, you not only contribute to groundbreaking research but also enjoy a range of benefits designed to enhance your life both inside and outside the workplace. 
 
As an equal opportunity employer, we prioritize fairness and respect, ensuring every team member thrives regardless of their background. But that's not all - our perks include:

28 days of annual leave plus local bank holidays and 4 dedicated wellbeing days.
Private Healthcare and Dental Coverage: Your health matters to us. Access top-notch medical and dental services, ensuring your well-being is in good hands.
Inclusive Culture: Be a valued member of our diverse, inclusive family. Your unique perspective is celebrated here, fostering a culture of mutual respect and understanding.
Health Assured: Your mental health is essential. Access our comprehensive mental health support services for a balanced work-life experience.
People’s Pension: Secure your future with our pension scheme, investing in your financial well-being beyond the workplace.

title: Data Enablement Officer
description:
At Efficio, we're not just a consulting firm; we're a team of dedicated experts committed to transforming procurement and supply chain functions. Our mission is to drive sustainable, measurable value for our clients through innovative solutions and deep industry insights. Join us and be part of a dynamic environment where your skills and ideas make a real impact.

Efficio is the world’s largest specialist procurement and supply chain consultancy, with offices across Europe, North America, and the Middle East. We’re a diverse team of over 1,000 individuals, representing more than 60 different nationalities and speaking 40+ languages – and we’re continuing to grow rapidly!

Data Enablement Officer

Help shape how Efficio uses data responsibly, securely and effectively.

We are looking for a Data Enablement Officer to establish and lead Efficio’s data governance framework, helping us protect client data while enabling its responsible use across our services, analytics, products and AI capabilities.

This is a highly visible role at the intersection of data, technology, AI, risk and client delivery. You will work across the business to turn complex contractual, regulatory, privacy and security requirements into practical guidance that enables teams to innovate with confidence.

Initially, the role will have a strong advisory and enablement focus: helping teams understand client requirements, assess new uses of data and make proportionate, risk-based decisions. As our governance model matures, the role is expected to take greater ownership of the framework and delegated authority for lower-risk decisions.

What you'll be doing

Establish our data governance framework

You will assess our current data-handling practices and develop a practical, scalable governance framework covering the lifecycle of client data – from collection and classification through to access, use, sharing, storage, retention and secure deletion.

You will develop and maintain policies and standards covering areas including:

  • Client data handling and classification

  • Data reuse and fair usage

  • Use of client data within Efficio products

  • Use of data with AI tools, including third-party and self-hosted solutions

  • Data access and security

  • Retention, archiving and secure disposal

  • Anonymisation and aggregation

  • Third-party data sharing

  • Policy exceptions and escalation

You will also help establish and maintain our information asset inventories, data flows and AI asset registers.

Enable responsible use of data and AI

A key part of the role will be helping teams determine what we can do with data, under what conditions, and with what safeguards.

You will establish a consistent approach for assessing new and changing data use cases, considering factors such as:

  • Why the data was originally obtained

  • Client and contractual restrictions

  • Data sensitivity and classification

  • The proposed use and intended recipients

  • Security and access controls

  • Retention requirements

  • Legal, client and reputational considerations

For AI use cases, you will help define which activities are permitted, restricted, require additional review or are prohibited. This will include the use of prompts, uploaded files and connected data sources, as well as expectations around human oversight, output validation and accountability.

Govern products, platforms and technology

You will define the conditions under which client data can be stored or processed using Efficio products, SaaS platforms, cloud services and AI tools.

Working closely with Technology, Information Security, Legal and Privacy teams, you will assess areas including:

  • Data residency and international transfers

  • Encryption, access controls and logging

  • Supplier and subcontractor access

  • Data retention, backups and deletion

  • Exit and data-export arrangements

  • Use of customer data for AI model training, product improvement or other secondary purposes

You will help ensure that unapproved platforms are not used for client data without appropriate assessment and documented approval.

Support new solutions and innovation

You will work alongside teams designing and deploying new data, software, analytics and AI solutions, providing governance input from an early stage.

Ahead of launch, you will help confirm that the appropriate governance, legal, privacy and security reviews have taken place and that material risks have been appropriately addressed.

Where issues remain, you will recommend practical remediation, escalation or, where necessary, a delay to rollout. Acceptance of significant residual risk will remain with the appropriate executive or governance committee.

Build governance that works in practice

This role isn't simply about writing policies. We want to create a governance model that teams can understand and use.

You will help develop:

  • A clear data governance operating model and decision-rights framework

  • Practical data, AI, security, reuse and retention policies

  • Data and AI use-case assessment processes

  • Risk-classification and escalation models

  • Policy exception processes and decision registers

  • Product and AI platform assessment standards

  • Solution launch-readiness checklists

  • Training, guidance and supporting materials

  • Governance reporting for senior leadership and relevant committees

You will coordinate, advise and constructively challenge stakeholders across the organisation while recognising that responsibility for managing data risk is shared across business owners, data owners, Legal and Privacy, Information Security, Technology and senior governance forums.

Client engagement

This will also be an important client-facing role.

You will participate in client discussions where required, confidently explaining Efficio's approach to data governance, security and responsible data use.

You should be comfortable responding to questions about how client data is accessed, used, stored, shared, retained and protected, translating technical or governance concepts into clear, credible explanations for different audiences.

What we're looking for

We are looking for someone with experience across one or more of the following areas:

  • Data governance or data management

  • Data privacy

  • Information security

  • Technology or operational risk

  • AI governance or responsible AI

You will also bring a practical understanding of modern technology environments, including SaaS, cloud, analytics and AI platforms.

You'll be someone who can operate comfortably between policy and practice – able to understand complex requirements while recognising the commercial and operational realities of a consulting and technology-enabled business.

In particular, you will be able to:

  • Translate complex regulatory, contractual and security requirements into practical business guidance

  • Apply proportionate, risk-based judgement rather than relying on a purely rules-based approach

  • Influence and challenge senior stakeholders constructively

  • Work effectively across Technology, Security, Legal, Privacy and business teams

title: Ingénieur R&D Conception d'équipements d’essais (H/F)
description:
Ingénieur R&D Conception d'équipements d’essais  (H/F)

À propos de notre client

Notre client est une TPE basée au nord de Lyon, spécialisée dans les énergies du sous-sol : pétrole, gaz, géothermie et stockage de CO2. Son activité repose entièrement sur la R&D : essais sur géomatériaux, géomécanique et développement d'équipements d'essais pour des clients internationaux.

Son équipe pluridisciplinaire et multiculturelle développe des solutions technologiques innovantes au service de l'efficacité, de la protection de l'environnement et de la maîtrise des coûts. L'entreprise est certifiée ISO 9001 et toutes ses activités respectent sa démarche QHSE.

Le poste

Pour accélérer ses projets de développement, notre client recrute un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D en conception d'équipements d'essais.  Vous prendrez en charge la conception, la mise au point et la validation de cellules d'essais haute température et haute pression, un sujet stratégique pour l'entreprise et ses clients.

Rattaché(e) à la direction des opérations, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe qui conçoit aujourd'hui les équipements et dépose les brevets de l'entreprise.

Répartition indicative du temps : environ 70 à 80 % conception et développement, 20 à 30 % laboratoire (montage et validation de vos équipements).

Dans une structure à taille humaine, vous suivrez vos développements de la conception jusqu'aux tests, avant leur transfert à l'équipe de production.

Vos missions

Conception et développement d'équipements d’essais

  • Concevoir de nouvelles cellules et de nouveaux dispositifs d'essais, notamment pour des conditions de haute température et de haute pression.
  • Résoudre les problématiques techniques associées : instrumentation et capteurs, étanchéité, tenue en température et en pression.
  • Consulter les fournisseurs et sous-traitants, et suivre la fabrication des pièces.
  • Améliorer les équipements existants, notamment leur ergonomie et leur facilité d'utilisation en production.

Mise au point et validation

  • Monter les équipements développés et réaliser leurs tests de validation au laboratoire.
  • Interpréter les résultats expérimentaux et vérifier leur cohérence.
  • Transférer les équipements validés à l'équipe de production et l'accompagner dans leur prise en main.

Documentation et propriété intellectuelle

  • Rédiger la documentation technique, les rapports et les comptes-rendus, et les présenter, en français comme en anglais.
  • Participer à la veille technique et à la rédaction des documents de protection (brevets, enveloppes Soleau).

Vie du laboratoire

  • Comprendre les essais réalisés au laboratoire pour concevoir des équipements adaptés à leurs besoins.
  • Contribuer à l'activité du labo et à l'amélioration continue, dans le respect de la démarche qualité ISO 9001.

Requirements

Compétences techniques

  • Conception mécanique et maîtrise d'un logiciel de CAO.
  • Instrumentation, capteurs et techniques de mesure.
  • Compréhension des grandeurs physiques et physico-chimiques.
  • Rédaction technique et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Savoir-être

  • Autonomie et capacité à prendre en main un sujet de bout en bout.
  • Rigueur, notamment dans les phases d'essais.
  • Polyvalence et goût du concret : vous aimez concevoir autant que tester vous-même vos équipements.
  • Communication proactive, en particulier pour remonter et résoudre les difficultés rencontrées.
  • Envie d'apprendre et de s'investir dans une petite structure.

Formation et expérience

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou équivalent Bac +5 en génie mécanique, conception, instrumentation ou mesures physiques.
  • Expérience d'environ 5 ans en conception d'équipements, en bureau d'études ou en R&D. Les profils plus juniors avec une première expérience significative en conception seront étudiés.
  • Une expérience sur des équipements soumis à des contraintes de température ou de pression est un vrai plus.

Benefits

Vous rejoindrez une entreprise à taille humaine où chaque développement compte : vos équipements seront directement utilisés pour des projets de R&D menés pour des clients internationaux. Vous travaillerez au sein d'une équipe dynamique et multiculturelle, sur des sujets techniques exigeants au service des énergies du sous-sol et de la transition énergétique.

Son équipe pluridisciplinaire et multiculturelle développe des solutions technologiques innovantes au service de l'efficacité, de la protection de l'environnement et de la maîtrise des coûts. L'entreprise est certifiée ISO 9001 et toutes ses activités respectent sa démarche QHSE.

Le poste

Pour accélérer ses projets de développement, notre client recrute un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D en conception d'équipements d'essais.  Vous prendrez en charge la conception, la mise au point et la validation de cellules d'essais haute température et haute pression, un sujet stratégique pour l'entreprise et ses clients.

Rattaché(e) à la direction des opérations, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe qui conçoit aujourd'hui les équipements et dépose les brevets de l'entreprise.

Répartition indicative du temps : environ 70 à 80 % conception et développement, 20 à 30 % laboratoire (montage et validation de vos équipements).

Dans une structure à taille humaine, vous suivrez vos développements de la conception jusqu'aux tests, avant leur transfert à l'équipe de production.

Vos missions

Conception et développement d'équipements d’essais

  • Concevoir de nouvelles cellules et de nouveaux dispositifs d'essais, notamment pour des conditions de haute température et de haute pression.
  • Résoudre les problématiques techniques associées : instrumentation et capteurs, étanchéité, tenue en température et en pression.
  • Consulter les fournisseurs et sous-traitants, et suivre la fabrication des pièces.
  • Améliorer les équipements existants, notamment leur ergonomie et leur facilité d'utilisation en production.

Mise au point et validation

  • Monter les équipements développés et réaliser leurs tests de validation au laboratoire.
  • Interpréter les résultats expérimentaux et vérifier leur cohérence.
  • Transférer les équipements validés à l'équipe de production et l'accompagner dans leur prise en main.

Documentation et propriété intellectuelle

  • Rédiger la documentation technique, les rapports et les comptes-rendus, et les présenter, en français comme en anglais.
  • Participer à la veille technique et à la rédaction des documents de protection (brevets, enveloppes Soleau).

Vie du laboratoire

  • Comprendre les essais réalisés au laboratoire pour concevoir des équipements adaptés à leurs besoins.
  • Contribuer à l'activité du labo et à l'amélioration continue, dans le respect de la démarche qualité ISO 9001.

Requirements

Compétences techniques

  • Conception mécanique et maîtrise d'un logiciel de CAO.
  • Instrumentation, capteurs et techniques de mesure.
  • Compréhension des grandeurs physiques et physico-chimiques.
  • Rédaction technique et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Savoir-être

  • Autonomie et capacité à prendre en main un sujet de bout en bout.
  • Rigueur, notamment dans les phases d'essais.
  • Polyvalence et goût du concret : vous aimez concevoir autant que tester vous-même vos équipements.
  • Communication proactive, en particulier pour remonter et résoudre les difficultés rencontrées.
  • Envie d'apprendre et de s'investir dans une petite structure.

Formation et expérience

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou équivalent Bac +5 en génie mécanique, conception, instrumentation ou mesures physiques.
  • Expérience d'environ 5 ans en conception d'équipements, en bureau d'études ou en R&D. Les profils plus juniors avec une première expérience significative en conception seront étudiés.
  • Une expérience sur des équipements soumis à des contraintes de température ou de pression est un vrai plus.

Benefits

Vous rejoindrez une entreprise à taille humaine où chaque développement compte : vos équipements seront directement utilisés pour des projets de R&D menés pour des clients internationaux. Vous travaillerez au sein d'une équipe dynamique et multiculturelle, sur des sujets techniques exigeants au service des énergies du sous-sol et de la transition énergétique.

As our new Key Account Manager, Public Sector, you will ensure the contract ownership, growth, and long-term success of strategic Public Sector accounts. Joining the Enterprise Account Management team, you will navigate the specificities of public procurement to drive local deployment and adoption. Your mission is to position Malt as a trusted partner while guaranteeing sustainable growth and alignment with our global enterprise strategy.

  • Own the execution of account strategies, including governance, deployment, and renewal for Public Sector entities.

  • Ensure strict compliance with public sector constraints, including specific procurement processes and contractual rigor.

  • Excellent negotiation skills with the ability to navigate complex budget cycles and procurement rules.

title: Junior Data & Automation Engineer
description:
Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning
 
Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team—from Finance to HR—to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Snowflake, Siemens, and DPD use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario.
 
With a team of 600+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software.
 
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo—all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

The Data & Automations Team

The Data & Automations team builds and operates Pigment's internal data platform, and designs, implements, and maintains the intelligent automation solutions that rely on it. Together, they streamline business processes and enhance data-driven decision making: we empower product, business and corporate functions through technology integration, robust data architecture, and process optimization, enabling teams to focus on high-value activities while ensuring accuracy and scalability.

The data platform is the foundation of everything we deliver. It is a centralized, governed ecosystem that collects, stores, transforms, and serves data to internal consumers across Product, Go-To-Market (GTM), and General & Administrative (G&A) functions, providing a single source of truth for analytics, automations, and AI. Making it reliable, secure, cost-efficient, and scalable is at the core of our mission. The team also consolidates and orchestrates AI efforts across Pigment, from governance and enablement to building AI-powered solutions.

Our team tackles diverse challenges, from integrating finance and HR systems and streamlining employee lifecycle processes, to building pipelines that turn product usage and customer interactions into actionable insights for Finance or GTM teams. AI is now at the center of most of what we do with data: many of our pipelines feed LLM-powered solutions, and the quality, structure, and governance of our data architecture directly determine what these solutions can deliver.

The team is led by Pigment's Deputy CISO and works closely with the Security team: security and data governance are part of how we build, not an afterthought.

Role

As a Junior Data and Automations Engineer, you will contribute to the continued development of Pigment's data platform: ingestion pipelines, dbt models, orchestration, data quality, and the underlying cloud infrastructure. You will also build and maintain the data pipelines, automations, and AI projects that support our G&A (Finance, People, IT) and GTM (Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships) teams.

You will work closely with senior engineers, starting with well-scoped tasks and progressively taking ownership of small projects end to end, from requirements gathering to production monitoring. This role involves collaborating with a wide range of internal stakeholders and requires excellent communication skills in English (primarily) and French, verbal and written.

Tech environment

Our core stack relies on Google Cloud Platform, maintained with Terraform, with components including BigQuery, Cloud Run, and Cloud Composer (Airflow), as well as dbt, Fivetran, Hightouch, Elementary for data observability, and Python for integrations and automations. Our pipelines connect business systems such as Salesforce, NetSuite, our HRIS, Gong, or Slack, and feed Pigment applications used by our own business teams. We also build LLM-powered pipelines and use AI tools in our daily engineering work.

You will have the opportunity to learn and grow your skills across these technologies while making a meaningful impact on Pigment's operational efficiency.

Key Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Data & Automations team's more senior members, you will participate in addressing the following topics.

Data Platform & Infrastructure:

  • Develop and maintain ingestion pipelines from APIs, databases, and SaaS tools, using Fivetran, Airflow, and Python
  • Build and maintain dbt models that turn raw data into clean, documented, and tested datasets
  • Contribute to the evolution of our orchestration, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code setup
  • Help improve data quality, observability, and alerting across the platform

G&A and GTM Data Pipelines & Automations:

  • Build pipelines and integrations that sync data between business systems (CRM, ERP, HRIS) through our data warehouse, including reverse ETL with Hightouch
  • Develop Python-based automations that remove manual work for teams such as Finance, People, IT, and Customer Success
  • Prepare reliable datasets for reporting and for the Pigment applications used by business teams

AI Projects:

  • Contribute to AI-powered solutions, such as LLM pipelines that extract, classify, and enrich unstructured data (call transcripts, messages, tickets)
  • Build the data foundations these projects rely on: AI-ready datasets, usage and observability data, evaluation data
  • Apply data architecture principles that make our data reliable, well-documented, and safely accessible for AI use cases (context, retrieval, access scoping)

Monitoring & Support:

  • Monitor pipelines and automations, troubleshoot incidents, and fix root causes
  • Document data models, pipelines, and processes for both technical and business readers

Collaboration & Learning:

  • Work with stakeholders - as diverse as Finance, People, Sales, and Product - to understand requirements and translate them into data solutions
  • Participate in code reviews and knowledge sharing sessions
  • Continuously expand your knowledge of data engineering, automation, and AI best practices

What you'll do
  • Under the supervision of the Business Automation team’s more senior members, you will participate in addressing the following topics.
    •  
    Automation Development:
  • Develop and maintain Python-based automations and solutions to streamline enterprise processes
  • Implement integrations between various systems and applications using APIs and other connection methods
  • Assist in maintaining CI/CD pipelines for automation projects
    •  
    Data Integration & Transformation:
  • Support the implementation of data pipelines that integrate data from various sources, including APIs, external databases, and third-party services
  • Assist in transforming raw data into clean and ready-to-use models using SQL and dbt
  • Collaborate on data quality monitoring and improvement initiatives
    •  
    Monitoring and Support:
  • Help implement monitoring for automation workflows and data pipelines
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues with existing automation solutions
  • Assist in documentation of systems, processes, and workflows
    •  
    Collaboration & Learning:
  • Work collaboratively with team members and stakeholders - as diverse as HR, Sales and Product Engineering - to understand requirements and implement effective solutions
  • Continuously expand knowledge of data engineering and automation best practices
  • Participate in code reviews and knowledge sharing sessions

    • Who you are

  • Technical skills

    The ideal candidate will possess most or all of the following qualifications. Hands-on experience through personal projects (share your GitHub account!), particularly contributions to open source initiatives, will be valued equally to professional and academic experience for this role.

  • Up to 3 years of relevant experience in data engineering, including apprenticeships, internships, and/or demonstrable personal projects
  • Strong SQL skills and understanding of data modeling concepts (e.g. layered or dimensional models)
  • Solid coding skills in Python
  • Understanding of ELT/ETL patterns, pipeline design, and data quality testing
  • Knowledge of version control systems (Git) and CI/CD concepts
  • Practical experience with a public cloud provider and a cloud data warehouse
  • Attention to detail and analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify edge cases
  • Good understanding of AI and LLM principles, along with practical use of AI tools in your work
  • Excellent communication skills in both French and English, written and verbal

    • Soft skills

  • Strong communication abilities - translating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and active listening skills for accurately capturing business requirements

About EH Group Engineering

EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

  • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

  • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

  • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

  • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

  • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

  • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

  • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

  • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

  • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

  • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

 

Skills and Experience Required:

  • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

  • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

  • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

  • Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

  • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

  • Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

  • Proven team player, with the ability to:
    (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
    (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

  • Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

  • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

  • Professional working language is in English.

     

Start date: Immediately

title: Responsable Qualité Multi-Sites - Piles à Combustible
description:
About EHG

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

 

EH Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

description:
About EHG

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

 

EH Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Robotics Integration Engineer
description:
About Enact

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role You Will

  • Design, integrate and test the electromechanical systems at the core of our dexterous robots: actuator modules, joints, and end-effectors, sensors, PCBs, and cable harnesses into compact, reliable units for high-DoF robotics

  • Bring hardware to life: lead system assembly & bring-up, debug across mechanics, electronics, and firmware, and work with controls & AI engineers to build a fully vertically integrated manipulation system

  • Develop & build automated test setups to validate performance, durability, and reliability, and take systems from prototype to series production

What We're Looking For

  • Degree (BSc/MSc/PhD) in mechatronics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field

  • 3+ years of work experience developing complex mechatronic systems that bridge mechanical design, electronics, and software

  • Solid understanding of electric motors, encoders, sensors, and motor drivers, and how to integrate them into a working system

  • Experience with system-level debugging and testing using tools such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, and data acquisition systems

  • Comfortable with programming for test automation and data analysis (e.g., Python)

  • Familiarity designing parts in CAD (e.g. Onshape)

  • Hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, workshop tools, soldering, 3D printing, and prototype assembly/testing

  • Fluency in English (spoken and written), with strong interpersonal and communication skills

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Hands-on development experience with high-DoF robotic systems (e.g., robotic arms, end-effectors, dexterous hands, or humanoids)

  • Development experience with actuator systems (frameless motors, gearboxes, encoders, and integrated drives)

  • Experience with motor control and communication buses such as EtherCAT or CAN

  • Experience with PCB design or schematic review, and cable harness design

  • Thermal management for compact, high-power electronics and actuators

What we offer

  • The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

  • A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

  • Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

  • Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity participation

title: DNA Synthesis Platform Engineer
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on scientist-engineer to help build our next-generation DNA synthesis platform, enabling high-throughput, cost-effective production of large and diverse DNA libraries. You'll work at the intersection of chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, and hardware development, designing and building prototypes, running experiments, and optimizing processes to turn new synthesis technologies into reliable, scalable production systems.

DNA synthesis is a fundamental part of our protein engineering platform. We're developing new approaches to dramatically increase synthesis throughput while reducing cost and turnaround time.

You'll work closely with our scientific and engineering teams to develop and prototype new DNA synthesis technologies. Your focus will be on translating scientific concepts into working hardware and experimental systems, designing and building prototypes, testing different approaches, and continuously improving their performance.

This is a highly hands-on, interdisciplinary role combining experimental science with practical engineering. You'll take ownership of prototype development, experimental validation, and process optimization, helping move promising technologies from early concepts to reliable, scalable systems.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, solving technical problems, and working across disciplines. You don't need to be an expert in DNA synthesis, but you should have strong scientific fundamentals, an engineering mindset, and experience turning ideas into working prototypes.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and test prototypes for next-generation DNA synthesis technologies.

  • Translate scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering designs and experimental setups.

  • Scope and evaluate different technical approaches, components, materials, and equipment for prototype development.

  • Develop and optimize the chemistry, materials, and processes underlying the synthesis platform.

  • Design and execute experiments to characterize performance, identify limitations, and improve reliability.

  • Work closely with mechanical, electronics, software, and automation engineers to develop integrated experimental systems.

  • Troubleshoot complex technical problems across chemistry, hardware, and process engineering.

  • Develop analytical methods and quality control strategies to measure performance and guide optimization.

  • Help scale successful prototypes into robust, reproducible systems suitable for routine production.

  • Work with external suppliers and engineering partners to source components, evaluate technologies, and accelerate development.

What We're Looking For

  • A strong background in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

  • Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing experimental setups, prototypes, or laboratory equipment.

  • Strong understanding of chemistry, materials, or process engineering, with the ability to apply these fundamentals to practical engineering challenges.

  • Experience developing and optimizing experimental processes, including systematic troubleshooting and performance characterization.

  • Comfortable working across hardware and experimental science, translating scientific requirements into practical engineering solutions.

  • Experience selecting components, evaluating technical trade-offs, and iterating on prototype designs.

  • Strong experimental skills, including designing experiments, analyzing data, and making decisions based on results.

  • Independent, resourceful, and comfortable working on open-ended technical problems.

  • A practical, hands-on approach to engineering, with a focus on building, testing, and improving systems rather than purely theoretical development.

  • Experience with DNA or oligonucleotide synthesis, including chemical or enzymatic approaches, is a plus.

  • Experience with solid-phase synthesis, surface chemistry, or chemical process development is a plus.

  • Familiarity with microfluidics, high-throughput dispensing, or array-based technologies is a plus.

  • Experience with laboratory automation, instrumentation, or custom hardware development is a plus.

  • Experience with CAD, electronics, fluidics, or mechanical prototyping is a plus.

  • Experience scaling experimental technologies from proof of concept to production is a plus.

  • Programming and data analysis experience, particularly in Python, is a plus.

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

title: Production Scientist (Senior)
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

This is not a lab technician position. This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline.

The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing.

This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities.

What You'll Do

  • Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time.

  • Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding.

  • Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them.

  • Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration.

  • Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff.

What We're Looking For

  • Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume.

  • PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or structural biology, plus 3-5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented.

  • Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result.

  • Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow.

  • Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works.

  • Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call.

  • Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production.

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

title: Senior Accounts Payable Coordinator
description:
ABOUT THE BRAND
 
At Karl Lagerfeld, we are driven by Karl’s mantra: “Embrace the present and invent the future.”
 
Always contemporary and forward-looking, the House of KARL LAGERFELD shares the creative vision and design aesthetic of its iconic founder, Karl Lagerfeld.
 
We are the only fashion house that carries Karl’s name on its door and we strive to live up to this responsibility in everything we do, every day, with the utmost joy and passion.
 
Our headquarters in Paris and in Amsterdam are home to a highly diverse and driven team of KARL family members that hail from over 35 countries. Together, we aim to create meaningful stories and product concepts that connect to Karl’s world and iconic attributes.
 
Women’s & Men's ready-to-wear, bags, small leather goods, swimwear and underwear are managed directly from our Amsterdam headquarters, while other categories, including footwear, fragrances, eyewear and more, are developed with best-in-class licensing partners.
 
We connect with our consumers on multiple levels, ensuring that our online and offline approach goes hand in hand. We thrive to maximize consumer engagement via more than 200 KL stores worldwide, our premium wholesale partners, and our strong digital footprint, spearheaded by our  karllagerfeld.com and 35 countries. Our digital channels currently represent more than 30% of our overall full-price business.
 
We are a dynamic, fast-growing and inclusive company built on professionalism and strong values. At KARL LAGERFELD we’re committed to working toward the highest standards of sustainability and integrity across all areas of our business,. In 2019, KARL LAGERFELD joined as a founding member of the Fashion Pact, a global sustainability initiative seeking to transform the fashion industry through objectives in three areas: climate, biodiversity and ocean protection.

THE ROLE

Are you looking to join a dynamic, fast-growing international fashion and retail company? We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Senior Accounts Payable Coordinator to support our Finance team. 

This role is responsible for managing the end-to-end accounts payable process, ensuring timely and accurate invoice processing, payment execution, vendor management, and compliance with internal controls.

The ideal candidate has experience working with Finance ERP, Medius AP Automation, and possesses a solid understanding of the Purchase Order (PO) lifecycle within a retail environment. You will thrive in a fast-paced international setting, demonstrate strong organizational skills, and maintain a high level of accuracy and professionalism.

Reporting directly to the Accounts Payable Team Lead, you will play a key role in supporting the financial operations of the business.

 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Invoice Processing & Vendor Management

• Process supplier invoices accurately and efficiently through Medius and M3, ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures.
• Perform thorough validation of invoice documentation and coding, allocating costs to the correct financial dimensions, entities, and cost center.
• Monitor and manage invoice workflows, ensuring timely approvals and resolution of exceptions.
• Maintain vendor master data, including the creation, modification, and validation of supplier records.
• Develop and maintain strong relationships with external vendors and internal stakeholders.

Purchase Order Management

• Review and validate invoices against approved Purchase Orders and Goods Receipts.
• Investigate and resolve PO-related discrepancies, including price variances, quantity mismatches, and missing receipts.
• Work closely with Procurement, Retail Operations, and business stakeholders to ensure adherence to the Purchase-to-Pay (P2P) process.
• Support continuous improvement of PO compliance and invoice automation processes.

Payments & Cash Management

• Prepare and process weekly payment runs, including both batch and manual payments, ensuring adherence to agreed payment terms.
• Respond promptly to supplier inquiries regarding payment status and account reconciliations.
• Record and reconcile bank transactions accurately within the accounting system.

Reconciliations & Controls

• Perform regular supplier statement reconciliations and proactively resolve discrepancies.
• Monitor AP aging balances and follow up on outstanding items to ensure timely resolution.
• Support month-end and year-end closing activities related to accounts payable.
• Ensure compliance with internal controls, financial policies, and audit requirements.
• Assist with internal and external audits by providing supporting documentation and responding to audit requests.

Team & Administrative Support

• Manage shared Accounts Payable mailboxes, ensuring effective communication and timely handling of requests.
• Process employee expense claims in accordance with company policies and approval procedures.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of Accounts Payable processes and finance operations.
• Support day-to-day Finance department activities as required.

THE PROFILE:

Experience & Knowledge

• Minimum 3-4 years of Accounts Payable experience, preferably within an international retail, fashion, or consumer goods environment.
• Hands-on experience with M3 ERP and Medius AP Automation is highly preferred.
• Strong understanding of the Purchase-to-Pay (P2P) process, including Purchase Orders, Goods Receipts, and invoice matching.
• Good knowledge of European VAT regulations and invoice compliance requirements.
• Experience with vendor reconciliations, payment processing, and month-end activities.

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
• Relevant accounting or Accounts Payable certifications are considered an advantage.

Skills & Competencies

• Strong analytical skills with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
• Ability to prioritize workload effectively and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Strong problem-solving capabilities and proactive mindset.
• Professional integrity with a commitment to confidentiality and compliance.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
• Fluent in English, both written and spoken; Spanish is a plus.

What We Offer

• The opportunity to work for globally recognized fashion and lifestyle brand.
• A collaborative and international working environment.
• Career development opportunities within a growing organization.
• Exposure to end-to-end finance operations and continuous process improvement initiatives.

description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for a senior B2B Growth Marketer to build and scale demand generation for ElevenLabs in the Benelux Region. This is a hands-on, in-region role focused on generating enterprise pipeline, growing our brand with technical buyers, and creating programs that become benchmarks for B2B marketing in AI.

As our first marketing hire in the Benelux Region, your work will shape how Benelux businesses discover, evaluate, and adopt ElevenLabs. The goal is to build repeatable marketing engines that make ElevenLabs the top choice for every enterprise.

 

What you'll do

  • Build integrated B2B marketing campaigns end to end across Benelux priority industries from strategy and messaging through execution and measurement.

  • Localize and execute programs across ABM, content, events, webinars, partner/customer marketing, executive branding, product launches, and outbound - choosing the right channel for the problem rather than owning a single function.

  • Adapt global campaigns and messaging for the the Benelux market, and feed local insights (buyer behavior, competitive dynamics, regulatory context) back to the global team.

  • Partner closely with local sales and the global product marketing, growth, and design teams to keep messaging consistent and execute high-impact campaigns.

  • Own pipeline generation and campaign performance for the market, using data to measure results, run experiments, and continuously improve what works.

 

Requirements

  • 4+ years of experience at a high-growth technology company - you've built and scaled B2B demand generation programs that created measurable enterprise pipeline, and you know what moved the needle.

  • Ownership Pedigree: You have implemented growth and marketing projects from start to finish and held yourself accountable for the ROI.

  • Deep knowledge of the Benelux market: its enterprise buyers, media landscape, and business culture, ideally with an existing network.

  • Work well without much process. This role spans multiple marketing functions and needs someone who sets priorities, spots opportunities, and moves quickly as our first marketer in the market.

  • Relentless commitment to excellence — a high bar for quality, clarity, and impact.

  • Curious about AI, follows the technology ecosystem closely, and has exceptional judgment on what makes marketing stand out.
